summary_short: Centene reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $53,579M, up 9.9% y/y, with net income of $1,091M swinging to a profit from a $253M loss a year earlier and diluted EPS of $2.19 versus a $0.51 per-share loss; the health benefits ratio improved to 89.6% from 93.0%.
summary_long: Revenue of $53,579M rose 9.9% y/y and 7.3% q/q, driven by PDP premium/membership growth, Marketplace and Medicaid rate increases, and risk-adjustment transfers, partly offset by lower Marketplace and Medicaid membership. The health benefits ratio fell to 89.6% from 93.0% y/y on improved Marketplace pricing/risk transfer, Medicaid cost management, and no 2026 Medicare Advantage premium-deficiency reserve add (versus one in 2025). Diluted EPS of $2.19 and net income of $1,091M both swung to a profit from a year-ago loss, though both fell versus Q1's $3.11 EPS. Cash rose to $24,151M (+66.4% y/y). Centene raised FY2026 guidance: total revenue to $193.5-197.5B, GAAP diluted EPS floor to >$3.11, adjusted diluted EPS floor to >$4.80.
